solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Salient point from Conservative leaving sales talk (4)

indicatorNotes.leaving: leaving means departing, so the C walks out of the word

blocks.note: C = Conservative, taken out of PITCH

annotation.surface: A political commentator picks out the key point once the Tory stops his sales patter.
annotation.walkthrough: C is the standard abbreviation for Conservative.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the soft core of a fruit gives the figurative sense of the central, most telling part of an argument.

entries.clue: Musical agent dealing with Topsy-Turvy supports one not working (11)

indicatorNotes.Topsy-Turvy: upside down: in a down entry the letters read bottom to top
indicatorNotes.supports: in a down entry, what supports sits underneath, so the reversed block goes below I

blocks.note: a rep is a sales agent

annotation.surface: A theatrical agent handling the Gilbert and Sullivan film Topsy-Turvy is propping up an out-of-work actor.
annotation.walkthrough: Topsy-Turvy is a real film about Gilbert and Sullivan, so it passes for the title of the musical; it is only the instruction to turn the first three words upside down.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a machine or rule that has stopped functioning or has no effect is described this way.

entries.clue: Fiery primate conceals archbishop’s first difficult issue (3,6)

indicatorNotes.conceals: to conceal is to hide, so POTTO hides the A inside it
indicatorNotes.first: take only the opening letter of archbishop

blocks.note: a potto is a small African primate
first letter of archbishop, placed inside POTTO

annotation.surface: A hot-tempered churchman hides the archbishop's first awkward problem.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Primate' wants to be a senior bishop, which suits archbishop; it is the animal, a potto.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: something too awkward to handle, passed quickly from person to person like a scalding vegetable.

entries.clue: Peter hit cops extremely tentatively in protective gear (6,4)

indicatorNotes.cops: to cop is to catch, so SAFE BELT catches the letters inside it
indicatorNotes.extremely: take the two extreme letters of tentatively

blocks.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe

annotation.surface: A man called Peter lashes out at police, though only half-heartedly, while wearing riot gear.
annotation.walkthrough: Peter looks like a man's name; in crosswords and old underworld slang it is a safe, hence a safecracker is a peterman.
annotation.definitionFit: A strap worn in cars and aircraft to restrain passengers during a crash counts as equipment that protects.

entries.clue: Some fail regularly following split (7)

indicatorNotes.regularly: at regular intervals, so take every other letter of fail
indicatorNotes.following: following means coming after, so these letters are placed after the split

annotation.surface: Some people keep failing after a break-up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Some' looks like the start of the surface sentence, but it is the whole definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both words stand before a plural noun for an unspecified handful, more than two but not many.

entries.clue: This topic should be avoided in Bedford (9,6)

blocks.note: IN BEDFORD rearranged, that is ground up

annotation.surface: A local warning that some subject is taboo in the town of Bedford.
annotation.walkthrough: The anagram indicator is the answer's own second word: FORBIDDEN is IN BEDFORD ground, crushed and remixed, so the answer describes its own wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: territory you may not enter, extended to a subject that conversation must steer around.

entries.clue: More neat French gentlemen in German city (7)

indicatorNotes.in: in means inside, so the gentlemen stand within the city's letters

annotation.surface: Some Frenchmen in a German city are more smartly turned out.
annotation.walkthrough: MM is the French abbreviation for Messieurs, gentlemen.
annotation.definitionFit: A comparative adjective: trim describes something tidy and well kept, and this form means more so.

entries.clue: Bird, say, on top of tree (5)

indicatorNotes.top of: in a down entry, the top of a word is its first letter

annotation.surface: A bird perches at the very top of a tree.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On' looks like a preposition about perching; it gives RE, meaning concerning.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: a white wading heron, one kind of bird among thousands.

entries.clue: Dryer in tall building changing hands (5)

indicatorNotes.changing hands: right hand is swapped for left: R becomes L

blocks.note: a tower; its R (right) changes to L (left)

annotation.surface: A clothes dryer is installed in a tower block that has just been sold.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Changing hands' reads as being sold; here the hands are right and left, R and L.
annotation.definitionFit: A cloth used after bathing removes water from skin, so it is literally a thing that dries.

entries.clue: Barman’s driven me to Barking (10)

indicatorNotes.Barking: barking means mad, so the letters are scrambled

annotation.surface: A publican complains that his customers have driven him to Barking, the London suburb.
annotation.walkthrough: Barking looks like the east London district; it is barking mad. A barman in crosswords is a composer, someone who writes bars of music.
annotation.definitionFit: A crossword-only sense: an Italian composer of madrigals and operas wrote his music in bars, so he is a barman.

entries.clue: Vaunted team (4)

blocks.note: boasted, the old past tense of crow
a group working together, on a ship or film set

annotation.walkthrough: 'The cock crew' is the older past tense of crow, and to crow is to boast or vaunt.
annotation.definitionFit: An archaic past tense of crow, to brag loudly, and also the people who work a ship or film set together.

entries.clue: Impressionist in US city starts to impersonate Romney (6)

indicatorNotes.starts to: the starts of words are their first letters

blocks.note: first letters of impersonate and Romney

annotation.surface: A comic impressionist in an American city is about to do an impression of Mitt Romney.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface's impressionist is a mimic, which suits impersonate; the answer is the painter.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the French painter of Luncheon of the Boating Party belonged to the movement of Monet and Degas.

entries.clue: Great time to enter base (8)

indicatorNotes.to enter: to enter is to go in, so the time letter goes inside the base word

annotation.surface: A fine moment arrives to set foot in the base camp.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Base' looks like a noun, somewhere to enter; it is the adjective, morally low.
annotation.definitionFit: Loose synonym: figures whose fame will never die, like sporting or literary legends, are called great.

entries.clue: Why battery’s replaced in holiday resort (11)

indicatorNotes.replaced: the letters are put back in a new order

annotation.surface: Someone on holiday wonders why the battery has been changed.
annotation.walkthrough: The fodder's two Ys and odd consonants point to Welsh spelling once you think of place names.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a university town on Cardigan Bay in west Wales, popular for seaside breaks.

entries.clue: Tennis legend finishing early for nothing (4)

indicatorNotes.finishing early: the word stops one letter short

blocks.note: Rafael NADAL without his last letter

annotation.surface: A tennis great retires early and gets nothing for it.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface nods to Nadal's actual retirement; 'finishing early' is literal, his name cut short.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional use: Spanish for zero, borrowed into American slang.

entries.clue: Light source shone out, constraining very exposed part of Tyrolean ensemble? (10)

indicatorNotes.out: out means wrong or disordered, so SHONE is rearranged
indicatorNotes.constraining: to constrain is to hold in, so the outer parts hold ER between them
indicatorNotes.exposed: exposed means stripped of covering, so very loses its outer letters

annotation.surface: A spotlight picks out the most revealing part of an Alpine band's costume.
annotation.walkthrough: Ensemble reads as a band of musicians; it is an outfit, and the question mark flags a definition by example.
annotation.definitionFit: Leather shorts with braces are one garment of traditional Alpine dress, so they are one piece of the outfit.

entries.clue: Getting better of those people interrupting continuously (2,3,4)

indicatorNotes.interrupting: to interrupt is to break in, so the pronoun breaks into the phrase for continuously

blocks.note: them = those people, inside ON END

annotation.surface: Someone recovering gets irritated by visitors who keep butting in.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Getting better of' reads as defeating someone; 'of' is only a link.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: a patient recovering from illness, or a situation improving, is said to be this.

entries.clue: Clergyman’s trifling argument against accepting article (5,5)

indicatorNotes.accepting: to accept is to take in, so the argument word takes the article inside

annotation.surface: A vicar raises a petty objection to taking on an item.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Article' reads as an item or piece of writing; in crosswords it is a, an or the.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: a priest attached to a cathedral who assists at services but is not on its governing chapter.

entries.clue: Smooth-talker in good spirits losing heart to member (7)

indicatorNotes.losing heart to: the middle letter is given up in exchange for what follows

blocks.note: cheer = good spirits; its middle E goes
an arm is a limb, a member; it takes the E's place

annotation.surface: A smooth operator in high spirits loses his heart to a club member.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Losing heart to' reads as falling in love; it means the heart of the spirits word is swapped for the member.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone who wins people over with flattery and easy conversation.

entries.clue: Close match one’s seen in bed (7)

blocks.note: a tie is a match, as in a cup tie

annotation.surface: A tight game being watched from bed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Close match' reads as one tight game; split it. A cup tie is a British term for a knockout match.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic hint: a woman's loose nightdress is the garment commonly worn when sleeping.

entries.clue: In Kyoto, your hat might be made of this (4)

annotation.definition: hat might be made of this

indicatorNotes.In: the answer lies inside the next words

annotation.surface: A tourist in Kyoto is told what local hats are made from.
annotation.walkthrough: Toyo is a Japanese straw-like material, so the surface's setting is the answer's origin too.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a shiny rice-paper straw from Japan woven into summer hats.

entries.clue: Elegant socialite broadcasting (8)

annotation.surface: A stylish society girl is on the radio.
annotation.walkthrough: A debutante is a young upper-class woman launched into society, shortened to deb.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: suave, stylish and confident in manner, usually said of a man.

entries.clue: Doctor can up quantity of saliva (5)

indicatorNotes.up: in a down entry, up reads bottom to top

blocks.note: can is slang for a toilet, a loo

annotation.surface: A doctor is able to raise the amount of spit collected for a sample.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Can' looks like a verb; it is the toilet, American slang, and a loo is the British word.
annotation.definitionFit: A noun use: the spit that dribbles from a baby's or dog's mouth.

entries.clue: Start living, having raised grand (5)

indicatorNotes.raised: in a down entry, the G is lifted higher up the word

blocks.note: BEING with its G taken out
G = grand, a thousand; put back higher, after BE

annotation.surface: Someone starts a new life after coming into a thousand pounds.
annotation.walkthrough: The G never leaves the word: BEING has its G moved up two places.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean to set something going or take the first step.

entries.clue: Arrive at nursing home, to begin with, in distinct part of town (6)

indicatorNotes.nursing: GET TO holds H like a nurse holding a patient
indicatorNotes.to begin with: only the first letter of home

blocks.note: first letter of home, inside GET TO

annotation.surface: Visiting a care home in a separate neighbourhood.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nursing home' reads as a care home; nursing is the container and home gives only its first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a district where one minority group lives, set apart from the rest of the city.

entries.clue: Some sleazy groper lying about in meeting of Congress (4)

indicatorNotes.Some: part of the words holds the answer

annotation.surface: A political scandal: a sleazy congressman lying about groping.
annotation.walkthrough: Congress, capitalised to look like the US legislature, is sexual intercourse.
annotation.definitionFit: A pun: congress in its old sense is sex, so a wild group session is a gathering for it.

entries.clue: Unknown number in Scotland know cycling in High Peak (5,5)

indicatorNotes.cycling: the first letter of AMOUNT goes round to the end
indicatorNotes.in: KEN and Y go inside MOUNTA

blocks.note: AMOUNT with its A cycled to the back

annotation.surface: Hikers in the Peak District come across an unknown number of Scots cycling.
annotation.walkthrough: High Peak is a real district of Derbyshire, which disguises the definition: a high peak.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Africa's second-tallest mountain, an extinct volcano on the equator.

entries.clue: Win card game in Panama? (4,6)

blocks.note: to land a prize is to win it

annotation.surface: Winning at cards while wearing a Panama hat.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: the isthmus of Panama joins two continents.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the isthmus is a narrow strip joining North and South America.

entries.clue: After party, nearly obtains port in Qatar (4)

indicatorNotes.nearly: nearly means not quite all, so the word falls one letter short

blocks.note: HAS, which means obtains, without its last letter

annotation.surface: After a party someone almost reaches a Gulf port.
annotation.walkthrough: A do is British slang for a party or celebration.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the capital city lies on the Gulf coast and serves as the country's main harbour.
